response.sql: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(*) AS number_of_orders FROM Customers AS c JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.gender) <> '' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender), shares AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, number_of_orders / SUM(number_of_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS share FROM customer_orders), compared AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS above_average_gap FROM shares) SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, above_average_gap FROM compared WHERE above_average_gap > 0 ORDER BY above_average_gap IS NULL, above_average_gap DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average is taken across all qualifying customers, regardless of gender.
NULL and blank gender values mean no gender was recorded.

alternatives.interpretation: Compare each customer's share with the average share among customers of the same gender.
